title: Fourier average under low-degree regularity
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\delta\in[0,1]$, and let $f$ be an odd real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube. Suppose $R\ge 0$ and every nonempty Fourier coefficient of $f$ indexed by a set of at most $t$ coordinates has absolute value at most $R$. Then, for every set $S$ of at most $t$ coordinates, the expected absolute Fourier coefficient indexed by $S\cap K$, where $K$ is sampled with the subset weights at parameter $1-\delta$, is at most $R$.
hypotheses_covered: Every nonempty Fourier coefficient indexed by a set of size at most $t$ has absolute value at most $R$
